title: Chain Reversal

story.briefing: The chain has to report back the way it came. Nothing can be re-linked in place down here, so the reversed order has to be produced by walking it once.
story.success: Chain reversed. The report travels back up the shaft in order.

description: Using the same chain format as before — an array of [value, next] nodes and a head index, with -1 ending the chain — return an array of the values in reverse order of traversal. An empty chain returns an empty array.
constraints: 0 <= nodes.length <= 300000, the chain never revisits a node
hints: You cannot reach the last node without walking the whole chain first, so the reversal has to happen after or during that walk.
Building the result by inserting each value at the front is correct but costs more the longer the chain gets. Collecting forwards and reversing once is cheaper.
Walk the chain collecting values into an array, then reverse that array — or walk it once and prepend, if you are happy with the cost. The forward-then-reverse route stays linear.
